html:
The Kot massacre took place in the courtyard of the palace armoury in Kathmandu, Nepal, on the night of 14 September 1846, when Jung Bahadur Kunwar and his brothers killed dozens of the leading nobles.

Jung Bahadur then made himself prime minister, took the name Rana, and made the post hereditary in his family. For over a century the Rana prime ministers ruled, while kings of the Shah dynasty were kept as figureheads. They sided with Britain, sending troops to crush the Indian rebellion of 1857, and kept Nepal shut to outsiders.

The Ranas built white stucco palaces in Kathmandu but few schools. In 1951 King Tribhuvan, backed by India and the Nepali Congress party, ended their rule. Democracy came slowly after, through the 1990 People's Movement.
